calibration.label: near-side box landmarks

quality_signal_definitions.label: Calibration valid
quality_signal_definitions.definition: Four-point calibration passed degeneracy, ordering, horizon and scale checks.
quality_signal_definitions.limitations: A valid homography can still be inaccurate far from the calibrated rectangle.

quality_signal_definitions.label: Camera drift vs calibration frame
quality_signal_definitions.definition: Max displacement of the calibration rectangle's corners between the reference frame and any sampled frame, from the validated frame-to-reference homography.
quality_signal_definitions.limitations: Only measurable when the motion model validates; zoom changes appear as drift too.

quality_signal_definitions.label: Pitch-line alignment
quality_signal_definitions.definition: Median over sampled frames of the share of detected pitch-line pixels that fall within 4 px of a reference-frame line pixel after mapping with the geometry used for projection.
quality_signal_definitions.limitations: White kit, shadows and line wear add noise; needs >=200 visible line pixels per frame.

quality_signal_definitions.label: Camera-motion inlier ratio
quality_signal_definitions.definition: Median MAGSAC inlier ratio of the frame-to-reference homography over sampled frames.
quality_signal_definitions.limitations: High ratios on a near-static camera are uninformative; crowd motion lowers it.

quality_signal_definitions.label: Camera-motion reprojection error
quality_signal_definitions.definition: Median (over frames) of the median inlier reprojection error of the motion homography.
quality_signal_definitions.limitations: Measured at half resolution and rescaled.

quality_signal_definitions.label: Frames with validated motion
quality_signal_definitions.definition: Share of sampled frames whose motion estimate (to the calibration frame, or chained) met inlier-count, ratio, error and sanity limits. Low = the calibration can no longer be verified for this segment.
quality_signal_definitions.limitations: A static camera over a texture-poor scene can also fail to validate; the agent then asks rather than assumes.

quality_signal_definitions.label: Projected locations outside pitch
quality_signal_definitions.definition: Share of detections whose foot is well inside the grass region (>=20 px from its edge) but whose projected ground point falls >3 m outside the pitch.
quality_signal_definitions.limitations: Assistant referees stand outside the touchline legitimately; grass-mask leakage can still admit edge spectators. Rises when calibration or camera geometry is wrong.

quality_signal_definitions.label: Implausible projected jumps
quality_signal_definitions.definition: Share of consecutive same-track observations implying a ground speed >12 m/s.
quality_signal_definitions.limitations: Far-field projection noise can produce false jumps; needs valid calibration.

quality_signal_definitions.label: Short (fragmented) tracks
quality_signal_definitions.definition: Share of tracks spanning < 1 s of the segment.
quality_signal_definitions.limitations: Players entering/leaving the view legitimately create short tracks.

quality_signal_definitions.label: Track fragmentation index
quality_signal_definitions.definition: Number of tracks divided by the median number of kept detections per sampled frame. ~1.0 means one track per visible player.
quality_signal_definitions.limitations: Inflated by view changes; deflated if the detector misses players consistently.

quality_signal_definitions.label: Association residual
quality_signal_definitions.definition: Median distance between a track's Kalman prediction and its matched detection, in box heights.
quality_signal_definitions.limitations: Low values do not prove correct identity: two players can swap with low residual.

quality_signal_definitions.label: Detection gaps
quality_signal_definitions.definition: Share of sampled frames with fewer than half the segment's median kept detections.
quality_signal_definitions.limitations: Occlusion by spectators in front of the camera is a natural cause the agent cannot fix.

quality_signal_definitions.label: Points far from calibration
quality_signal_definitions.definition: Share of projected player points more than 30 m from the calibrated rectangle (informational).
quality_signal_definitions.limitations: Homography error grows with distance from the calibrated area.

teams.note: Team labels come from jersey colour clustering; confidence is a heuristic agreement score, not a probability.

A.caveat: Computed from players visible in this camera view only (typically fewer than 11); a partial view understates true team width/depth. Positions >30 m from the calibrated rectangle carry larger projection error.

heatmap.definition: Each observation of a player inside the pitch adds the segment's sampling interval (stride / fps seconds) to the 5 m x 5 m cell containing its projected ground point.
